extracted.intended_audience: mathematicians and applied mathematicians (authors, students, researchers) preparing papers, theses, talks, posters, software reports, and career documents
extracted.subtask_description: Practical style, structure, and procedural guidance for producing mathematics and numerical-analysis writing and associated artifacts (papers, theses, slides, posters, code/data, CVs, referee letters). Emphasizes audience-driven choices, mathematical notation, reproducibility, and LaTeX best practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of handbook
rubrics_metrics.description: Covers all writing tasks faced by a mathematician or applied mathematician: papers, theses, books, slides, posters, web pages, blog posts, referee reports, CVs, grant proposals, recommendation letters, email.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the handbook as a single reference covering both prose and technical/algorithmic reporting, plus career documents and interactions with editors/referees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choose your journal first
rubrics_metrics.description: Choose your journal first. Style is downstream of audience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decide the target venue early; conformity to its expectations should shape title, level of background, notation choices, and length.

rubrics_metrics.name: English style
rubrics_metrics.description: English style: Active voice, short sentences, concrete nouns, strong verbs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer active constructions, avoid long or convoluted sentences, minimize abstract nominalizations; cut unnecessary adjectives/adverbs (e.g., 'essentially', 'basically', 'very').

rubrics_metrics.name: Inline versus displayed formulas
rubrics_metrics.description: Inline vs. displayed formulas — rules of thumb.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Display long or unwieldy formulas; use inline formulas only when short and not disrupting sentence flow. Consider readability and punctuation when deciding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Punctuation of displayed formulas
rubrics_metrics.description: Punctuation of displayed formulas — punctuate them as English.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat displayed equations as part of the sentence: end with commas/periods as appropriate and make grammatical sense in context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notation: mnemonic, consistent, sparse
rubrics_metrics.description: Notation — mnemonic, consistent, sparse.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose symbols that suggest meaning, use each symbol for a single purpose, avoid overloading and excessive sub/superscripts; maintain a single source of truth for symbol definitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subscripts and superscripts
rubrics_metrics.description: Subscripts and superscripts — minimize stacking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid deep stacks of indices that hinder readability; simplify notation or introduce definitions to reduce stacking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pseudocode conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Pseudocode conventions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt clear pseudocode style (consistent indentation, meaningful variable names, clear control structures) so that algorithms are unambiguous and readable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting numerical experiments (table contents)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reporting numerical experiments — what tables must contain (problem size, machine, software version, timing units).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Every result table should include problem size, hardware, software version, units for timing, and any relevant parameters so results are interpretable and comparable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reproducibility for numerical work
rubrics_metrics.description: Reproducibility — code and data archived with the paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Archive code and data (with versions and instructions) alongside the publication; reproducibility is described as non-negotiable for numerical research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cite the original source
rubrics_metrics.description: Cite the original source, not the textbook.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When possible find and cite the primary reference that introduced a result rather than a secondary source or textbook.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid vague review citations
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid 'for a review see X' without naming X precisely.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If referring to a review, identify which review and why it is relevant rather than a throwaway 'for a review see ...' phrasing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use BibTeX and check entries
rubrics_metrics.description: Use BibTeX; check entries by hand.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Manage references with BibTeX for consistency, but verify each entry for accuracy (authors, titles, pages, years, DOIs) and completeness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tables and figures: captions and labeling
rubrics_metrics.description: Each figure needs a self-contained caption; axes labeled with units; logarithmic axes labeled 'log'; color-blind safe palettes; legible at print resolution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Captions should let the figure be understood without reading the main text; ensure axes have units, label log axes clearly, choose color palettes accessible to color-blind readers, and verify readability at expected print/display sizes.

rubrics_metrics.name: TeX and LaTeX usage (math typesetting)
rubrics_metrics.description: TeX and LaTeX usage: Use \cdot for products; \,d for differentials. Don't \mathbf bold variables that should be italic. Use \text inside math mode for English words. Macro hygiene; one source of truth per symbol.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow semantic TeX conventions for math spacing and text, avoid stylistic hacks (bolding variables), centralize symbol definitions with well-named macros to ensure consistency across the document.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Title length and content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose a concise title that conveys main topic and scope; tailor phrasing to the journal and audience to attract appropriate readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Abstract = self-contained.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make the abstract a standalone summary of problem, main results/contributions, and significance; avoid undefined notation and unexplained acronyms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Introduction guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Introduction includes literature, motivation, contribution, structure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the introduction to set context and motivation, cite relevant literature, state clearly what the paper contributes, and outline the paper structure to guide the reader.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conclusion guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Conclusion is not a summary; it is forward-looking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the conclusion to discuss implications, future directions, and open problems rather than merely restating results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Talks and slides
rubrics_metrics.description: Talks and slides: One idea per slide. Title bar = thesis sentence. Avoid full sentences on slides. 1 minute per slide rule of thumb. Practice; time it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design slides to emphasize a clear narrative: each slide should support a single point, the slide title should state the takeaway, minimize text, and rehearse to match timing expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Posters
rubrics_metrics.description: Posters: Visible from 2 m away. Reader's path is a U or Z; mark it. Title 1, abstract 0; figures dominant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Layout posters for remote legibility (large fonts, clear figures), guide the reader through a marked visual path, minimize abstract text, let figures and captions carry the message.

rubrics_metrics.name: Working with an editor/referee
rubrics_metrics.description: Working with an editor / referee: Acknowledge every comment in the response letter. Fight only for what matters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respond to reviewers point-by-point, acknowledging and addressing comments; be selective in disputing suggestions—prioritize substantial issues over stylistic disagreements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Career documents: CV, cover letter, statement
rubrics_metrics.description: Career documents: CV: chronological, complete, no jargon. Cover letter: target the institution. Statement: research arc with one sentence per paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep CVs thorough and chronological; tailor cover letters to the institution and position; structure research/teaching statements clearly—summarize papers succinctly and explain the research trajectory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Have a thesis; state it
rubrics_metrics.description: Have a thesis; state it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Formulate a clear central message or thesis for the paper early and make sure each part contributes to it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Know your reader
rubrics_metrics.description: Know your reader.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Write at the appropriate level of background and detail for the intended audience; choose examples, notation, and emphasis accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cut unnecessary modifiers
rubrics_metrics.description: Cut adjectives, adverbs, 'essentially', 'basically', 'very'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eliminate filler words and vague qualifiers that weaken clarity and precision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Symbols are nouns; use words for verbs
rubrics_metrics.description: Symbols are nouns; use words for verbs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid overusing symbols in place of verbs or logical connectors; write readable sentences where operations and relations are clear.

rubrics_metrics.name: Display unwieldy formulas
rubrics_metrics.description: Display unwieldy formulas; punctuate them as English.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a formula is complex or disrupts sentence flow, display it and ensure surrounding punctuation and grammar are correct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notation must be unique
rubrics_metrics.description: Notation must be unique (one symbol = one meaning).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not reuse symbols for different concepts; define notation explicitly and avoid ambiguity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tables and figures are first-class citizens
rubrics_metrics.description: Tables and figures are first-class citizens; caption them fully.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat visual elements as essential content—make them self-contained with informative captions and ensure they are integrated into the narrative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cite primary sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Cite primary sources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer primary literature for attribution of results and credit; avoid relying solely on textbooks or secondary summaries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reproducibility is non-negotiable in numerical work
rubrics_metrics.description: Reproducibility is non-negotiable in numerical work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide sufficient information (code, data, parameters, hardware/software details) to allow independent reproduction of numerical experiments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revise multiple times; read aloud
rubrics_metrics.description: Revise multiple times; read aloud.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Iteratively edit drafts and read text aloud to catch awkward phrasing, errors, and issues of flow and emphasis.
